title: The 10 Best Corded Rotary Hammers
subtitle: SDS-Plus rotary hammers for concrete and masonry, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: A rotary hammer drills concrete, brick, and block much faster than a regular hammer drill, and most can switch to hammer-only mode for chipping tile or mortar. We ranked 10 corded SDS-Plus best-sellers on rating, review volume, and features (vibration control, a slip clutch, and bits and chisels in the box). They run from a $53 8-amp starter kit to a $240 Bosch with a kickback sensor.

products.name: DEWALT SDS Plus Rotary Hammer Drill, 1-1/8 in., Vibration Control, Corded (D25263K)
products.verdict: The one to buy if you drill concrete more than once in a while: an 8.5-amp D-handle hammer with DEWALT's SHOCKS vibration control, a clutch that lets go when a bit jams, and a 3-year warranty. Sold and shipped by Amazon.
pros: SHOCKS active vibration control at the handles
Clutch cuts the sudden torque reaction when a bit binds
Longest warranty on the list: 3 years, plus 2 years of free service
Works with DEWALT's D25301D dust extractor
cons: No bits or chisels in the box, just the side handle, depth rod, and kit box
The listing doesn't state the tool's weight or number of modes

products.name: BOSCH 11255VSR Bulldog Xtreme 1 In. SDS-Plus Rotary Hammer
products.verdict: The most-reviewed name-brand rotary hammer on Amazon, with 3,000+ ratings at 4.7 stars. Three modes, 0-1,300 rpm, 0-5,800 bpm, and a 36-position Vario-Lock for setting the chisel angle.
cons: Hits lighter than the DEWALT (2.0 ft-lb)
The listing doesn't mention a slip clutch
1-year warranty on this listing
No bits included

products.name: Makita HR2641 1" AVT Rotary Hammer, Accepts SDS-Plus Bits (D-Handle)
products.verdict: Makita's AVT counterweight system cancels much of the hammering vibration, and a torque-limiting clutch protects the gears if the bit binds. A pro-grade D-handle with 40 chisel angle settings.
pros: Anti-Vibration Technology counterbalance plus a damper spring
40 bit angle settings and a retractable tool hook
cons: Far fewer reviews than the DEWALT and Bosch
1-year warranty on this listing
No bits included

products.name: BOSCH GBH2-28L 8.5 Amp SDS-plus Bulldog Xtreme Max 1-1/8 In. Rotary Hammer
products.verdict: Bosch's step-up Bulldog adds KickBack Control, a sensor that stops rotation when the bit binds, on top of counter-balanced vibration control. Worth the extra money if you drill overhead or all day.
pros: KickBack Control sensor stops the tool on bind-up
cons: Most expensive hammer on the list
Sold by a third-party seller (Express Shipping Tools), not Amazon
No bits included

products.verdict: The most-reviewed hammer on the list at 3,500+ ratings, and the hardest hitting at 5.5 ft-lb. A heavy 13-amp tool for breaking tile and chiseling concrete, with bits, chisels, and a case in the box.
pros: Safety clutch and double-layer vibration damping
Comes with 3 bits, 2 chisels, grease, and a case

Sold by the brand's store, not Amazon

products.verdict: Another 13-amp, 1-1/4 inch demolition-style hammer with a full accessory kit. Same price as the ENEACRO, with fewer reviews and a thinner spec sheet.
pros: 13-amp motor for chipping and tile removal
3 bits, 2 chisels, spare brushes, and a case included

12 lb, so it's a two-handed tool

products.verdict: The best-selling rotary hammer in our search, at 1,000+ sold a month. At 7.2 lb it's the lightest tool here, and it has a clutch, reverse, and a lock-on trigger for about $55.
pros: Lightest on the list at 7.2 lb
3 bits, 2 chisels, and a case included

3 bits, 2 chisels, depth gauge, and case included

avoid.name: DOVAMAN 1-9/16'' SDS Rotary Hammer Drill, 12.5Amp Heavy Duty (RH15A)
avoid.flag: Headline 1-9/16" is its wood capacity; spec table says 230 V
avoid.verdict: The headline number is misleading and the spec table contradicts the bullets. For about the same money, the ENEACRO has near-identical published specs, a consistent listing, and a stated 2-year warranty.
reasons: The title leads with 1-9/16", a size buyers associate with bigger SDS-Max hammers. The bullets show that's the wood capacity. In concrete, which is what a rotary hammer is for, it's rated at 1-1/4", the same as the $110 ENEACRO and AOBEN.
The spec table lists 230 volts and 12.5 milliamps. The bullets say 120 V and 12.5 amps. Some of the published numbers are wrong, and the listing doesn't tell you which.
Its published dimensions, bare-tool weight, and 18.1 lb kit weight almost exactly match the ENEACRO ENRH3201's, so you'd pay the same price for what reads as the same tool under another label.
It's sold by a third-party storefront (MilkyWay Galaxy), not the brand, and the listing states no warranty term.

buyers_guide.a: A hammer drill uses ridged clutch plates to rattle the bit. That's fine for a few 1/4" anchor holes in brick. A rotary hammer uses a piston to strike the bit, so it drills concrete several times faster, handles 1/2" and larger holes easily, and can chip in hammer-only mode. If you're drilling more than a handful of holes in concrete, get a rotary hammer.

buyers_guide.q: What is SDS-Plus, and do I need special bits?
buyers_guide.a: SDS-Plus is the shank and chuck system on every hammer on this page. The bit slides in and locks without a key, and it can slide back and forth so the piston can strike it. You need SDS-Plus bits and chisels. Regular round-shank bits won't fit without an adapter chuck, and SDS-Max bits are a larger, different size.

buyers_guide.q: How much impact energy do I need?
buyers_guide.a: Around 2 to 3 joules (1.5 to 2.2 ft-lb) handles anchor holes up to about 1/2" and light tile removal. The 13-amp hammers rated 5 to 7 joules are better for breaking floor tile, chiseling concrete, and holes over 3/4", but they weigh 12 lb or more. Brands don't all measure impact energy the same way, so treat small differences between brands with some skepticism.

buyers_guide.q: Is vibration control worth paying for?
buyers_guide.a: If you'll run it for more than a few minutes at a time, yes. Hammering vibration is what wears out your hands and arms. DEWALT's SHOCKS, Makita's AVT, and Bosch's counter-balance systems cut what reaches the handle; many budget tools only add a padded grip.

buyers_guide.q: Why don't the name-brand hammers include bits?
buyers_guide.a: DEWALT, Bosch, and Makita sell the tool with a side handle, depth rod, and case, and expect you to buy bits for the job. A decent SDS-Plus bit and chisel set runs $30 to $40. The budget brands bundle bits and chisels, which is handy for a first project, but those bits tend to wear out quickly.

buyers_guide.q: What does a safety clutch do?
buyers_guide.a: If the bit catches on rebar or jams in the hole, the motor's torque can twist the tool hard enough to hurt your wrist. A slip clutch or kickback sensor disconnects the drive when that happens. Every pick here lists one except the Bosch 11255VSR, whose listing doesn't mention it.
